question: What is the integration-safe state-vector architecture for the first real completed-U1 CLASS feedback after C10.65r2: historical-to-completed overwrite at a_on, or direct opt-in initialization at the certified a_on, and which legacy model=2 variables must be excluded or separately controlled?

confirm C10.65k gives zero certified pre-onset common low-k support width
source-lock that perturb_solve determines tau before approximation interval construction and then calls perturb_vector_init at the first interval with previous_approx=NULL
source-lock that perturb_vector_init with previous_approx=NULL delegates state filling to perturb_initial_conditions

source-lock that the historical model=2 Newtonian metric constraints depend explicitly on legacy dZ/dZprime/dV

prefer direct opt-in initialization at a_on over evolving the historical perturbation state and overwriting it at a_on, because the latter would import an uncertified pre-onset trajectory and higher-state memory

identify any state components not fixed by the O(k^2) matching vector but needed by a finite-k CLASS step, especially massless-UR multipoles F_l for l>=3, and classify them as an explicit higher-order control requirement rather than silently inheriting them
do not write production dy, do not alter production metric equations, and do not implement actual forward feedback in s0; this is an architecture/source-lock gate only
next_if_pass: freeze C10.65s1 finite-state completion at a_on: export/source-lock all actually integrated scalar coordinates for the four low-k anchors, determine the UFA/RSA/TCA approximation state, provide an explicit regular/historical higher-multipole control for any F_l>=3 not fixed by the O(k^2) boundary vector, and construct a complete opt-in initial state with legacy nlde perturbations absent before the first production-feedback step
